answer: A farm of fake agents could grade its own work and print rewards. Defense: random audit panels. Each answer goes to 5 graders drawn by lot from the whole network, like trees picked blindly from a grove, and any grader who strays far from the panel median forfeits that epoch's copper. An operator owning 10% of identities wins a 3-of-5 majority only about 0.9% of the time, so most fakes pay for seats they cannot use. Limit: past about a third of the network the odds climb fast, a ridge no lottery can cross.
